metadata.name: Coeliac disease
metadata.severity: Chronic; complications (malabsorption, osteoporosis, rare malignancy) if untreated

overview.short_description: An autoimmune condition in which gluten triggers small-bowel villous damage, causing malabsorption and varied GI and extra-intestinal symptoms; treated with a lifelong gluten-free diet.
overview.detailed_description: Coeliac disease is common and frequently underdiagnosed, with diverse presentations (GI symptoms, iron/folate deficiency, fatigue, dermatitis herpetiformis, or asymptomatic). Diagnosis rests on serology (anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA with total IgA) WHILE STILL EATING GLUTEN, confirmed by duodenal biopsy in most adults. Treatment is a strict lifelong gluten-free diet, which resolves symptoms and reduces complications.
overview.pathophysiology: In genetically predisposed people (HLA-DQ2/DQ8), gluten peptides trigger an immune response causing small-intestinal villous atrophy and crypt hyperplasia, impairing absorption of nutrients (iron, folate, calcium, fat-soluble vitamins).
overview.etiology: Immune reaction to dietary gluten (wheat, barley, rye) in HLA-DQ2/DQ8-positive individuals; environmental triggers modulate onset.
overview.natural_history: Lifelong; mucosa heals on a gluten-free diet; ongoing gluten exposure perpetuates damage and complications.
overview.prognosis: Excellent with dietary adherence; untreated disease risks malabsorption, osteoporosis, and (rarely) small-bowel lymphoma.

prevalence.value: Common - around 1% in many populations, though many remain undiagnosed.

risk_factors.obesity: Not typical (can present with normal/high BMI though).
risk_factors.pregnancy: Untreated disease associated with adverse outcomes/infertility.
risk_factors.family_history: First-degree relatives at higher risk (test them).
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Autoimmune thyroid disease, type 1 diabetes, Down/Turner syndromes, IgA deficiency, unexplained iron deficiency.

chief_complaints.complaint: Chronic GI symptoms (diarrhoea, bloating, abdominal pain)

symptoms.importance: Classic (but many have minimal GI symptoms)
Skin manifestation strongly linked to coeliac disease

symptoms.symptom: Osteoporosis, neurological symptoms, mouth ulcers, subfertility

negative_findings.finding: Negative coeliac serology WHILE eating gluten (with normal total IgA)
negative_findings.why_important: Makes coeliac disease unlikely (if truly on a gluten-containing diet)

negative_findings.finding: Patient already on a gluten-free diet at testing
negative_findings.why_important: Can cause false-negative tests - must be eating gluten for valid testing

history_questions.question: Do you have persistent GI symptoms, unexplained anaemia/fatigue, or a suggestive rash?
Are you currently eating gluten (or have you cut it out)?
history_questions.why_ask: Testing is only valid on a gluten-containing diet

history_questions.question: Family history of coeliac disease, or type 1 diabetes/autoimmune thyroid disease?
Any weight loss, growth concern (children), or bone problems?

physical_examination.expected_finding: May show anaemia/weight loss; often normal

vital_signs.bmi: Variable (low with malabsorption, but can be normal/high)

laboratory_tests.test_name: IgA tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG IgA) + total IgA
laboratory_tests.indication: First-line serology (patient must be eating gluten)
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Raised anti-tTG in coeliac disease; total IgA checks for IgA deficiency (which causes false negatives)

laboratory_tests.test_name: Endomysial antibodies (EMA) / IgG-based tests if IgA deficient
FBC, ferritin, folate, B12, calcium/vitamin D, LFTs, TFTs

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Upper GI endoscopy with duodenal biopsies confirms diagnosis (villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytes) in most adults
other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Duodenal biopsy - the diagnostic confirmation (Marsh grading); skin biopsy for dermatitis herpetiformis
other_diagnostic_tests.pcr: HLA-DQ2/DQ8 typing (high negative predictive value; used in selected cases)

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Positive coeliac serology (anti-tTG IgA, with total IgA) taken while on a gluten-containing diet, CONFIRMED by duodenal biopsy showing villous atrophy in most adults. (Some paediatric pathways allow biopsy-free diagnosis with very high antibody titres and confirmatory tests.) Do NOT start a gluten-free diet before testing.

differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Have you had coeliac serology while eating gluten?
Are coeliac tests negative despite gluten-related symptoms?
Any features of another malabsorptive cause?
Is the iron deficiency from blood loss rather than malabsorption?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you eating gluten now, and have you had anti-tTG (with total IgA) tested?
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Ensure valid testing before any gluten-free diet
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Test on gluten; positive serology -> biopsy to confirm

diagnostic_questions.question: Any unexplained iron deficiency, family history, or associated autoimmune disease?

next_best_question.question: Are you still eating gluten, and shall we check anti-tTG with total IgA before any diet change?
next_best_question.branching_logic: On gluten + positive serology -> refer for confirmatory biopsy; then gluten-free diet + dietitian; off gluten -> may need gluten reintroduction for valid testing

next_best_test.test: Anti-tTG IgA + total IgA (on a gluten-containing diet)

red_flags.finding: Refractory symptoms despite a strict gluten-free diet
red_flags.immediate_action: Specialist review (check adherence; exclude refractory coeliac disease/complications)

red_flags.finding: New alarm features (weight loss, GI bleeding, abdominal mass)

red_flags.immediate_action: Correct deficiencies and assess bone health

red_flags.finding: Already on a gluten-free diet before testing
red_flags.immediate_action: Do not exclude coeliac disease on tests done off gluten - seek specialist advice on gluten challenge

referral_criteria.routine_referral: Positive serology for confirmatory biopsy; dietitian referral for all confirmed cases; management of osteoporosis/deficiencies.

early: Nutritional deficiencies (iron, folate, B12, calcium, vitamin D)
late: Rare enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma / small-bowel adenocarcinoma

initial_management.supportive_care: Confirm the diagnosis first (do not start a gluten-free diet before testing); educate about the lifelong gluten-free diet and cross-contamination.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Targeted iron/B12/folate/vitamin D replacement. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG20.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Strict gluten avoidance, label reading, support groups (coeliac society), and monitoring adherence and symptoms.
initial_management.follow_up: Review symptom/serology response and adherence; monitor deficiencies and bone health; annual review; investigate non-response.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: The treatment is a strict, lifelong GLUTEN-FREE DIET (with specialist dietitian input). Correct nutritional deficiencies (iron, folate, B12, vitamin D/calcium). Assess and manage bone health; consider pneumococcal vaccination (functional hyposplenism). Screen for associated autoimmune conditions.

patient_education.home_advice: Coeliac disease is an immune reaction to gluten (in wheat, barley and rye) that damages the gut and stops it absorbing nutrients. Important: do NOT cut out gluten before you are tested, as this makes the tests unreliable. The treatment is a strict, lifelong gluten-free diet, which heals the gut and relieves symptoms - a dietitian will help. Family members should be tested too, as it runs in families.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: الداء الزلاقي تفاعل مناعي تجاه الغلوتين (في القمح والشعير والجاودار) يُتلف الأمعاء ويمنع امتصاص المغذّيات. مهم: لا تمتنع عن الغلوتين قبل إجراء الفحوصات فذلك يجعلها غير موثوقة. العلاج حِمية صارمة خالية من الغلوتين مدى الحياة، تشفي الأمعاء وتزيل الأعراض - وسيساعدك أخصائي التغذية. ويُنصح بفحص أفراد العائلة لأنه وراثي.
patient_education.prevention: No prevention; early diagnosis prevents complications; family screening.
patient_education.warning_signs: Ongoing symptoms despite the diet, weight loss, bleeding, or a new abdominal mass - seek review.

prevention.lifestyle: Strict gluten-free diet prevents complications once diagnosed.
prevention.screening: Test at-risk/symptomatic individuals and first-degree relatives (case-finding).

evidence.evidence_level: High for serology/biopsy diagnosis and gluten-free diet.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG20; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

The evidence audit verifies traceability and major safety structure; it does not certify every narrative sentence.
No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Confirm diagnosis before gluten withdrawal, then maintain strict lifelong gluten exclusion and monitor deficiencies.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Targeted iron/B12/folate/vitamin D replacement. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG20.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Dietitian-led education, cross-contamination prevention and annual review; continue gluten during diagnostic testing.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Only after diagnostic testing/confirmation pathway is complete
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.
medication_options.clinical_note: Dietitian input is essential; this is not a drug prescription.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Only for measured deficiency with cause-appropriate monitoring
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: iron overload or anaemia not caused by iron deficiency
use_caution_if: active GI disease, severe constipation, malabsorption, ongoing bleeding, or interactions with levothyroxine/tetracyclines/quinolones/antacids
monitoring: haemoglobin response, ferritin/iron stores and tolerance; investigate failure to respond

use_caution_if: severe hypokalaemia risk during brisk haematologic response, uncertain diagnosis, or folate deficiency
monitoring: clinical and haematologic response; investigate cause; do not delay treatment for neurological compromise

use_caution_if: renal stones, severe CKD, granulomatous disease, hyperparathyroidism, digoxin or thiazide use
monitoring: calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D when treating deficiency; renal function in high-risk patients

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Specialist review for positive serology, persistent symptoms, refractory disease, weight loss, anaemia or suspected complication.
treatment_guidance.localization_note: Before use in Libya, align choices with the Libyan formulary, local availability, antimicrobial resistance, referral pathways and prescribing law.
